limitations: The managed session is admitted only for an exact Workbench-created disposable Prism projection with a completed V3 launch receipt.
GroovyScript 1.4.3 accepts one active language client at a time and reopens the same port after that client disconnects.

The upstream endpoint has no cryptographic identity challenge; Workbench strengthens the binding through a reserved public endpoint, a checked upstream port, checked overlays, exact launch custody, and process observation.
When Workbench runs in WSL and Prism runs on Windows, the descriptor binds a managed stdio TCP bridge, a distinct Windows upstream port, and explicit local-to-server workspace URIs.
The readiness canary proves initialize and canonicalization diagnostics before handoff; it does not execute pack scripts or prove effective registry state.
Cancellation first requests a window close when available and then escalates only against session-owned process identities.
